preview_en:
Bosnia and Herzegovina look to build on a successful World Cup as they embark on their UEFA Nations League (UNL) opener against a Poland side who have dropped into League B for the first time.

Match News and Current Form

Poland may have missed out on their first World Cup since 2014 due to a 3-2 play-off final loss to Sweden in March, but that was their only loss in seven competitive matches under Jan Urban (W4, D2) which indicates an upward trajectory. Still led by 38-year-old record scorer Robert Lewandowski, the Eagles are looking for a positive response to relegation in the previous UNL cycle (W1, D1, L4), with this the first time they’ve dropped down into the second tier. Poland should fancy their chances here on home soil too, having lost just one of their last nine fixtures as hosts (W6, D2).

It’s been a historic year for Bosnia and Herzegovina, who beat Wales and Italy in qualifying play-offs to reach just a second-ever World Cup finals. Progressing to the knockout stages in the summer marked the Dragons’ greatest achievement, and in this international window they’ll say goodbye to their greatest ever player as Edin Džeko retires. He’ll hope to help his side to a strong start to their UNL campaign after relegation in 2024/25, with Bosnia having been promoted from both prior cycles in which they participated in League B.

Head-to-Head History

Poland are unbeaten in all five prior H2Hs (W4, D1), winning both previous competitive meetings in the 2020/21 UNL cycle.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Just three of Poland’s last nine home matches produced over 2.5 goals.

Poland won the corner count in five of their last six competitive internationals.

Excluding neutral turf, Bosnia are unbeaten in their last five away games (W3, D2), the last four of which saw both teams score.

Bosnia have scored more than once in only one of their prior 12 UNL League A games.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Lewandowski boasts 12 goal involvements in 16 UNL appearances (G4, A8), with half of his personal goal haul coming in 2020/21’s corresponding fixture. Haris Tabaković has started the season in inspired form with ten goals in 12 games for Salzburg and has scored in four of his last five Bosnia appearances, with three of those strikes coming after half-time.

Kamil Grabara is absent from Poland’s squad with a long-term knee injury while Jakub Moder is also out. Amar Dedić is not with the Bosnia squad after aggravating an injury while playing for club side Newcastle.

Betting Analysis

Considering their status as sizeable outsiders, backing Bosnia in the double chance market holds plenty of appeal here after a superb year.

Author: Ryan Fisher
